lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Answer the Health Inspector About Lucía's Breakfast
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Answer formal questions about the breakfast incident and correct any errors in the written statement.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are Lucía's friend, and the AI is food-safety inspector Amparo Ferrer: answer her formal questions about the breakfast using usted, and go through your written statement line by line to confirm or correct it, using passive se such as se sirvió and ¿cómo se comunica…?
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Formal register; passive se for procedures (se sirvió a las ocho; ¿cómo se comunica la información de alérgenos?)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: Excuse me, there's a wrong time in the second section.
Where it says 8:30, it should say 8:10.
How is allergen information communicated to customers?
Could it be corrected before I sign?
With that correction, I agree with the statement.
Could you provide me with a copy of the report, please?
I'd rather not state anything I didn't see myself.
Is the allergen record checked every morning?

sourcePassageEnglish: Two days later, the health inspector Amparo Ferrer meets with Emma and the manager Vicente at the hotel.
Amparo brings Emma's written statement about her friend Lucía's allergic reaction to the almond sponge cake.
Amparo: We are going to review your statement section by section before closing the inspection report.
Emma: The first section is correct, because Lucía mentioned her almond allergy when she arrived at the buffet.
Emma: Excuse me, there's a wrong time in the second section.
Emma: Where it says 8:30, it should say 8:10.
Vicente: According to the hotel's schedule, the sponge cake was served at 8:00, which is its usual serving time.
Emma: Could it be corrected before I sign?
Amparo: Of course, it's a typo and it gets corrected right now.
Amparo: How is allergen information communicated to customers?
Vicente: A card listing the allergens is placed next to each dish at the buffet.
Vicente: In addition, the dining-room staff receives monthly training on our allergen protocol.
Amparo: Did you see the card next to the sponge cake that morning?
Emma: I'd rather not state anything I didn't see myself.
Amparo: Is the allergen record checked every morning?
Vicente: Yes, the head chef checks it and writes down the batch of the almond flour to maintain traceability.
Emma: With that correction, I agree with the statement.
Emma puts her signature at the end and then asks: Could you provide me with a copy of the report, please?

lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Répondre avec courtoisie à des questions formelles et corriger uniquement les faits que l’on peut confirmer.
lessons.focusEnglish: Formal French questions and impersonal procedure wording: How was the information recorded? Could the time be corrected?
lessons.focusFrench: Questions formelles et tournures impersonnelles : Comment les renseignements ont-ils été consignés ? Pourrait-on corriger l’heure ?
lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: This fictional interview does not assert legal authority, inspection rules, allergen compliance or a duty to sign. Witness may decline to attest to unseen facts.

english: Two days after the breakfast incident, Emma returns to a hotel in Québec City.
A person introduced as an inspector meets Emma and the duty manager.
The inspector asks Emma to review a draft of her own statement.
Emma says that she will confirm only what she witnessed.
The first section describes when Emma arrived in the breakfast room.
Emma checks her notes and says the section matches them.
In the next section, she notices a different time.
Emma says her note records eight ten, not eight thirty.
She asks for the time to be corrected before she approves the wording.
The inspector marks the requested correction for review.
The manager mentions a kitchen ingredient record.
Emma says she did not see that record and cannot confirm its contents.
The inspector asks how ingredient information was recorded that morning.
The manager says he will check the records with the kitchen team.
Emma rereads the corrected timeline and asks for one phrase to stay neutral.
She does not agree to a cause she cannot verify.
She asks for a copy of her statement before deciding whether to sign it.
The inspector thanks her for distinguishing observation from uncertainty.
french: Deux jours après l’incident du petit-déjeuner, Emma retourne dans un hôtel à Québec.
Une personne présentée comme inspectrice rencontre Emma et le responsable de service.
L’inspectrice demande à Emma de relire un projet de sa propre déclaration.
Emma dit qu’elle confirmera seulement ce dont elle a été témoin.
La première section décrit l’heure à laquelle Emma est arrivée dans la salle du petit-déjeuner.
Emma consulte ses notes et dit que la section leur correspond.
Dans la section suivante, elle remarque une heure différente.
Emma dit que sa note indique huit heures dix, et non huit heures trente.
Elle demande que l’heure soit corrigée avant d’approuver la formulation.
L’inspectrice note la correction demandée pour vérification.
Le responsable mentionne un registre des ingrédients de la cuisine.
Emma dit qu’elle n’a pas vu ce registre et ne peut pas en confirmer le contenu.
L’inspectrice demande comment les renseignements sur les ingrédients ont été consignés ce matin-là.
Le responsable dit qu’il vérifiera les documents avec l’équipe de cuisine.
Emma relit la chronologie corrigée et demande qu’une phrase reste neutre.
Elle n’accepte pas qu’on indique une cause qu’elle ne peut pas vérifier.
Elle demande une copie de sa déclaration avant de décider si elle la signera.
L’inspectrice la remercie de distinguer les observations des incertitudes.

lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Email the Hotel a Written Incident Summary
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Write a clear, formal summary of the incident and your requests, sharing only the health details Lucía approved.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are drafting the email to Inés Soler, and the AI is Lucía, your friend: read your summary aloud, check which health details she approves, and organize it with en primer lugar, a continuación, sin embargo, por lo tanto and por último.
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Written register; report connectors (en primer lugar, a continuación, sin embargo, por lo tanto, por último)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: Dear Ms. Soler: I am writing regarding what happened on Tuesday.
First of all, I would like to thank your staff for their quick response.
Below, I briefly summarize what happened during breakfast.
However, the allergen menu was not on display.
Therefore, I request a written reply about what happened.
Finally, I look forward to your reply.
Lucía, is it OK if I mention that you went to the ER?
I won't include anything from the medical report without your permission.

sourcePassageEnglish: In her room at the hotel in Valencia, Emma writes the summary of the incident for Inés Soler, the customer service manager.
In the subject line she puts: Allergic reaction at breakfast on Tuesday, October 13.
Lucía, her friend, is sitting on the bed and decides which health information she wants to share with the hotel.
Emma: Lucía, is it OK if I mention that you went to the ER?
Lucía: Yes, but don't mention the diagnosis or the medications, please.
Emma: I won't include anything from the medical report without your permission.
For Lucía, confidentiality is important, so her consent only covers the almond allergy and the visit to the ER.
Dear Ms. Soler: I am writing regarding what happened on Tuesday.
First of all, I would like to thank your staff for their quick response.
Below, I briefly summarize what happened during breakfast.
During our stay, my friend ate a sponge cake with almond, had an allergic reaction and went to the ER.
However, the allergen menu was not on display.
Therefore, I request a written reply about what happened.
I also ask for an apology and a review of the allergen menu within a time frame of 15 days.
I am attaching a copy of the official complaint form that we filled out at the front desk.
Finally, I look forward to your reply.
Before sending the email, Emma checks the attachment and confirms that it does not include the medical report.
For the sign-off, Emma writes: Sincerely, Emma Clarke.

Lucía, is it OK if I mention that you went to the ER?
Below, I briefly summarize what happened during breakfast.
Therefore, I request a written reply from you.
I am attaching a copy of the official complaint form.

sourceGrammarExamplesEnglish: First, my friend had an allergic reaction during breakfast.

lessons.titleFrenchCourseEnglish: Rédiger un suivi avec le consentement de son amie
lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Organiser un courriel formel, vérifier les faits et ne partager que les renseignements personnels autorisés.
lessons.focusEnglish: Formal written sequence: first, next, however, therefore, finally; check consent before sending.
lessons.focusFrench: Connecteurs de courriel formel : tout d’abord, ensuite, toutefois, par conséquent, enfin ; vérifier le consentement avant l’envoi.
lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: The writer does not infer a cause, include medical records, promise a remedy, or assume a legal complaint process.

words.en: Dear Ms. Roy, I am writing about Tuesday’s breakfast.
words.fr: Madame Roy, je vous écris au sujet du petit-déjeuner de mardi.

words.fr: Je ne joindrai aucun renseignement médical sans ton accord.

passage.titleFrench: Rédiger un suivi avec le consentement de son amie
english: In Montréal, Emma drafts a follow-up email to the hotel after the breakfast incident.
Her friend Léa sits beside her and decides which details may be shared.
Emma asks whether she may mention that Léa left with medical responders.
Léa agrees to that fact but does not want other health details in the email.
Emma confirms she will not attach any medical document.
She writes a neutral subject line about the breakfast follow-up.
First, she thanks the staff for responding that morning.
Next, she lists what she witnessed in chronological order.
She notes what Léa ate but does not infer why she felt unwell.
Emma says she did not see how the cake was prepared.
She asks the hotel to verify the ingredient and preparation records.
She requests a written reply and asks when one might be available.
She does not demand a specific remedy or promise one.
Léa reads the draft and asks Emma to remove one unnecessary personal detail.
Emma removes it and checks the message again.
They confirm the attachment contains only Emma’s own notes.
Emma ends with a polite closing and her name.
She sends the email only after Léa approves the final wording.
french: À Montréal, Emma rédige un courriel de suivi à l’hôtel après l’incident du petit-déjeuner.
Son amie Léa est assise à côté d’elle et décide quels détails peuvent être partagés.
Emma demande si elle peut mentionner que Léa est partie avec les secours médicaux.
Léa accepte que ce fait soit mentionné, mais ne veut pas d’autres renseignements de santé dans le courriel.
Emma confirme qu’elle ne joindra aucun document médical.
Elle écrit un objet neutre pour le suivi du petit-déjeuner.
Tout d’abord, elle remercie le personnel d’être intervenu ce matin-là.
Ensuite, elle énumère dans l’ordre chronologique ce dont elle a été témoin.
Elle note ce que Léa a mangé, sans déduire pourquoi elle s’est sentie mal.
Emma dit qu’elle n’a pas vu comment le gâteau a été préparé.
Elle demande à l’hôtel de vérifier les documents sur les ingrédients et la préparation.
Elle demande une réponse écrite et souhaite savoir quand elle pourrait être disponible.
Elle n’exige pas de mesure précise et n’en promet aucune.
Léa relit le projet et demande à Emma de supprimer un détail personnel inutile.
Emma le supprime et vérifie encore le message.
Elles confirment que la pièce jointe contient seulement les notes d’Emma.
Emma termine par une formule de politesse et son nom.
Elle n’envoie le courriel qu’après l’accord de Léa sur la formulation finale.

lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Text a Casa Rural Host When the Train Runs Late
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Text and then call a host to explain a delay, change the group size and ask politely about breakfast times.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are on a delayed train to Asturias, and the AI is Begoña, the casa rural host: text her that the group grew from 3 to 5, then call to ask about breakfast times with le escribo porque…, ¿le vendría bien…? and ¿podría guardarnos el desayuno?
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (¿le vendría bien…?, ¿podría guardarnos el desayuno?, te escribo porque…)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: the connection (change of train or bus)
Good afternoon, Begoña, I'm writing because the train is running late.
In the end we'll be 5 instead of 3, would that work for you?
Could you save breakfast for us until 10:30, if it's no trouble?
Sorry, it's cutting out; we're going through a tunnel.
I'll call you back as soon as I have signal.
Would you mind leaving the keys in the lockbox for us?
Would it be possible to have breakfast a little later tomorrow?
Guys, Begoña is saving breakfast for us until 10:30.

sourcePassageEnglish: Daniel is traveling by train to Asturias with his friends to spend the weekend at a rural guesthouse in Cangas de Onís.
The ticket inspector walks through the car and announces that the train is 1 hour late because of a breakdown.
With this delay they are going to miss the train change in Oviedo, so the arrival time in Cangas de Onís changes quite a bit.
Also, there is a change of plans, because Lucía and her brother Pablo joined the trip this morning and now there are 5 of them.
Daniel writes a message to Begoña, the owner of the house: Good afternoon, Begoña, I'm writing because the train is running late.
In the same message he adds: In the end we'll be 5 instead of 3, would that work for you?
Begoña answers with a voice message: no problem, because she can put an extra bed in each room.
Half an hour later, Daniel sees a missed call from Begoña and calls her right away.
Daniel: Would it suit you if we arrived around 23:00?
Begoña: That works for me, but at that time I won't be at the house anymore.
Daniel: Would you mind leaving the keys in the lockbox for us?

Begoña explains to him that the key lockbox is next to the door and that, since Cangas de Onís has no train station, from the Arriondas station they can take the ALSA bus, about 15 minutes, or a taxi from the stand out front.
Daniel politely asks her what time she serves breakfast, and Begoña answers that it is usually from 8:00 to 10:00.
Daniel: Could you save breakfast for us until 10:30, if it's no trouble?
Suddenly, Begoña's voice sounds broken up because the train goes into a tunnel.
Daniel: Sorry, it's cutting out; we're going through a tunnel.
When he has signal again, Daniel calls her once more and Begoña confirms that she will save breakfast for them.
Daniel: Guys, Begoña is saving breakfast for us until 10:30.

Begoña is saving breakfast for us until 10:30.
Begoña can put in an extra bed.

sourceGrammarExamplesEnglish: I'm writing because the train is 1 hour late.

lessons.titleFrenchCourseEnglish: Prévenir une hôte d’un retard de train
lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Écrire puis appeler une hôte pour annoncer un retard, demander si deux personnes de plus peuvent venir et vérifier les horaires du petit-déjeuner.
lessons.settingEnglish: French rural guesthouse after a delayed TER trip
lessons.focusEnglish: Polite text and telephone requests: I am writing because the train is late; would five guests be possible?
lessons.focusFrench: Demandes polies par message et téléphone : je vous écris parce que le train a du retard ; serait-il possible d’accueillir cinq personnes ?

passage.titleFrench: Prévenir une hôte d’un retard de train
english: Daniel and two friends are traveling by regional train to a rural guesthouse in France.
The conductor announces a delay that may affect their connection.
Daniel checks the booking and sees that it is for three guests.
Two more friends ask whether they can join the trip.
Daniel tells them that the host must confirm before the booking changes.
He writes to the host, Claire, to explain the train delay.
He asks whether a reservation for five would be possible.
Claire replies that she needs to check the rooms before answering.
Daniel receives a missed call while the train passes through a tunnel.
When the signal returns, he calls Claire back.
He asks how to collect the keys if the group arrives late.
Claire describes the guesthouse check-in arrangement for this booking.
Daniel also asks about the usual breakfast hours.
He asks whether a later breakfast might be possible the next morning.
Claire says she will check staffing and reply in writing.
Daniel repeats the details he has understood without treating them as a confirmed change.
He tells his friends that the group size and breakfast request are still pending.
They wait for Claire’s confirmation before making new travel plans.
french: Daniel et deux amis voyagent en train régional vers une maison d’hôtes rurale en France.
Le contrôleur annonce un retard qui pourrait perturber leur correspondance.
Daniel vérifie la réservation et voit qu’elle est prévue pour trois personnes.
Deux autres amis demandent s’ils peuvent se joindre au voyage.
Daniel leur dit que l’hôte doit confirmer avant toute modification de la réservation.
Il écrit à l’hôte, Claire, pour expliquer le retard du train.
Il demande si une réservation pour cinq personnes serait possible.
Claire répond qu’elle doit vérifier les chambres avant de répondre.
Daniel reçoit un appel manqué pendant que le train traverse un tunnel.
Quand le réseau revient, il rappelle Claire.
Il demande comment récupérer les clés si le groupe arrive tard.
Claire explique les modalités d’arrivée prévues pour cette réservation.
Daniel demande aussi les horaires habituels du petit-déjeuner.
Il demande s’il serait possible de prendre le petit-déjeuner plus tard le lendemain matin.
Claire dit qu’elle vérifiera la disponibilité du personnel et répondra par écrit.
Daniel répète les détails qu’il a compris sans les présenter comme une modification confirmée.
Il dit à ses amis que le nombre de personnes et la demande de petit-déjeuner sont encore en attente.
Ils attendent la confirmation de Claire avant de modifier leurs projets de voyage.
